A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PHASE-Net work and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Content can be matched despite extensive reformatting and relocation of the lighting analysis.

before.justification: v1 reports original PHASE-Net benchmark results, domain-generalization experiments, component ablations, lighting-robustness measurements, and predicted waveforms.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in its main text and supplementary material, including Tables 1–4 and the ablation and waveform figures.

M1.justification: The ZAS spatial permutation, ASF spatial weighting and temporal-derivative concatenation, gated TCN, and negative Pearson correlation objective remain unchanged. The rewritten methodology overview does not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use UBFC-rPPG, PURE, BUAA-MIHR, and MMPD with the same task and scenario coverage. The lighting scenarios in v3 Section 4.3 were already evaluated in v1 Appendix F.

E2.justification: TS-CAN is removed from the efficiency comparison between v1 Table 4 and v3 Table 5. Other comparator sets are retained. The efficiency row labeled MDNet (Ours) becomes PHASE-Net (Ours), correcting its identification rather than adding a method.

E3.justification: The reported intra-dataset, leave-one-out, and two-source transfer protocols and MAE/RMSE/R metrics remain unchanged. Appendices A–B retain the same data selection, input dimensions, and training settings. New average columns summarize existing experiments.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same component removals, TCN-depth and loss-weight sweeps, ZAS parameter analyses, and waveform examples. The lighting analysis moves into the main text, and ZAS plots are combined without changing the questions tested or supporting evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new averages across source combinations are result summaries, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 Tables 3–4 add averages of the unchanged limited-source results: PHASE-Net has MAE/RMSE/R of 10.99/16.50/0.28 on MMPD and 3.48/5.21/0.89 on BUAA-MIHR. The TS-CAN efficiency entry, 7.50M parameters and 96.0G MACs, is removed. Retained benchmark scores, ablation results, lighting measurements, and waveform images are unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 removes Section 3.2's explicit ZAS time-complexity characterization, O(B*k*T*H*W). The dynamical derivation, convolution and FIR propositions, ZAS mathematical properties, and Appendix C–D proofs and generalization bounds otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central physics-grounded architecture, accuracy, generalization, and efficiency claims remain. However, v3's conclusion drops the assertion that PHASE-Net is readily adaptable to other video-based biomedical applications, modestly narrowing its stated applicability.

C2.justification: v3 removes the explanation that zero-FLOP ZAS still incurs indexing runtime while retaining the zero-computational-cost wording, making its efficiency interpretation less qualified. The main mechanism explanations, result interpretations, and exclusion of extremely dim BUAA recordings remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a source-code repository link in the abstract and identifies the UBFC waveform examples as subjects 22 and 9 in Figure 6. Appendix B's implementation, hyperparameters, and H100 hardware information are unchanged. The linked code itself was not inspected.

R1.justification: v3 adds six cited works covering extreme-lighting rPPG, spike sorting, class-incremental learning, face reenactment, facial-expression analysis, and causal reinforcement learning. These are citation additions without substantial new discussion; the positioning against heuristic architectures and physics-informed losses remains.

P1.justification: v3 merges the traditional and deep-learning related-work subsections, rewrites the methodology overview and observation-model explanation, and moves lighting robustness into Section 4.3. It also updates front matter and adds acknowledgments. Most prose and the overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted into two columns with separately headed supplementary material. v1 Table 3 becomes two redesigned tables with source-combination columns and averages; the ZAS figures are merged, the lighting figure moves into the main text, and waveform panels gain individual labels. Several plots are substantially reduced in display size.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves usability and reproducibility documentation through the code-access pointer, correction of the MDNet efficiency-row label, and clearer per-target transfer tables with accurate averages. These gains do not strengthen the underlying empirical validation or proofs. Smaller ablation and waveform plots and removal of the indexing-runtime qualification partly offset the improvement.
